correctness.rationale: For every complex t != 0, each conic-line restriction has exact discriminant 8(t-8); the conic meets one of the four finite line vertices exactly when t=16 and neither infinite vertex ever. This exhausts singularities via pairwise intersections and Bézout, giving 14 A1 / 6 A1+4 A3 / 2 A1+4 D4 and Tjurina totals 14/18/18. The coefficient matrices of all homogeneous Jacobian relation maps in degrees 1..4 were exactly reduced to Smith form over QQ[t]. Their invariant factors establish for ALL complex t the mdr values 4/3/2 (the degree-1 injectivity also rules out degree-0 relations). A standalone checker reconstructs the matrices and verifies each Smith invariant, both explicit low-degree syzygies, discriminants and vertex incidence equations. Gałecka Theorem 3.2 then gives nearly free precisely at t=8,16, while the standard degree-6 free-curve exponent and Tjurina formula excludes freeness. No finite sample is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical concentric smooth-conic deformation of the explicit four-square-line arrangement used as a degree-six nearly-free example. Geometrically dictated radii t=8 (inscribed circle tangent to all four sides) and t=16 (circumscribed circle passing through four vertices) generate distinct singularity types but identical Tjurina number, with different exact mdr values and near-free exponents. The complete classification establishes how a nearly-free special fiber sits in its natural deformation and proves that one other, essentially different near-free fiber exists while the open complement is not nearly free. This is a natural family-wide rank and singularity stratification, not a routine isolated number check.
